Then I give you this vase to a friend, and I see this vase at the friend's home. He puts flowers in it, and he’s very happy with this vase. This gives me satisfaction because I can see my impact in the world.

Okay. Amber would have been for you the mediator between you and the species, thus between and thus being felt by you and acknowledged as a completion of your own essence and a necessary part of yourself. By doing so, I would thereby have realized that I was confirmed both in your thought and in your love.

In this way, this vase now shapes your reality, and I know it has given you meaning and shaped your reality. Therefore, I find meaning in that.

This is a very Frankish attitude where you can project your imagination onto people and shape the way they see reality. This concept is similar to what we are discussing here.

In my expression of my life, I would have fashioned your expression of your life. In doing so, I have realized my own essence, my human communal essence.

So this is something that sounds perfectly correct because it becomes a basis for our society. The idea of individualism and materialism underpin these concepts.

In such a situation, our products would be like many mirrors, each one reflecting on our essence. Thus in this relationship, what occurred on my side would also occur on yours.

He's saying that objects become mirrors where we can see our own individuality reflected. This goes against the religious concept where humanity is all reflected in each of us. He's creating a material outlook by denying the existence of God and spirituality while applying religious concepts to a material world.

He recognizes that we have these spiritual religious needs, but he argues we don't need God to achieve them; materialism can fulfill these needs. This is a very Frankish concept.

My work would be a free expression of my life, therefore a free enjoyment of it. In work, the peculiarity of my individuality would be affirmed since it is an extension of my individual life. Work would thus be genuine active property, presupposing private property and the externalization of my individuality. My activity is torment to me because I hate it, seeing only its appearance as a force imposed by external arbitrary needs.

Right? So why would transnational capital support this idea? Before the debate was mind versus matter. What matters more—the spirit or the flesh? Marx says no; the dialectic is between private property and public property. In private property, I work for someone else, but in public property, I work for myself. This is the question that defines the debate.

So trans capital uses this idea to make us think only private versus public matters, advancing empire by turning us all into slaves.

Marx is correct in analyzing capitalism’s problems. But his problem is believing the solution is making capital public, leading to a workers' paradise. However, history isn't linear; capitalism won’t naturally lead to socialism or communism.
